messages:
Sam Torres: FYI perf spike after yesterday's kernel swap, seeing host-side p95 jump ~18% for short-chat workloads. Repro locally with a small harness.
Maria Chen: Ugh. Is this during steady batching or minibatches?
Sam Torres: Mini-batches (batch size 1-4), steady QPS. Kernel selector picked the new 'fast-attn-v2' variant on sequences <128 which I thought would help.
Jordan Patel: Any KV cache thrash? Could be kvcache miss pattern with the new kernel's memory access.
Sam Torres: I profiled and attached flame snippets (perf-bot uploaded: link internal/perf/1764141414/flame.svg). Host parse + tokenization time increased from ~0.9ms -> 1.5ms median in the repro.
Leo Kim: That sounds like parsing path, not GPU. Can you paste the hot functions?
Sam Torres: Hot stack (top-down):
  - ingress::parse_frame
  - tokenizer::slice_and_norm
  - hostio::serialize_chunks
  - kernel_bridge::prepare_kv_shard
  - rpc::grpc_writev
Maria Chen: serialize_chunks + grpc_writev is suspicious. We changed writev batching recently. Maybe the kernel change changed packetization frequency.
Jordan Patel: Could also be header fragmentation: new kernel reduces token emission per step -> more small writes. Any metrics on writev counts per request?
Sam Torres: Yes. Before: avg writev calls/request ~2.1. After: ~3.8. Smallwrite ratio up from 12% -> 43%. P99 latency increase correlates with increased syscall counts.
perf-bot: Regression alert: host_p99_latency increased by 22% (window: 2026-03-20T02:00 -> 2026-03-20T08:00). Suspected contributing tags: kernel=fast-attn-v2, seq_len_bucket=<128, batching=minibatch
Maria Chen: So kernel change indirectly increased fragmentation on host framing. Two levers: prefer kernel that emits larger chunks, or coalesce at proxy layer.
Sam Torres: I ran quick experiment: force kernel selector to prefer legacy-attn for seq<128 and writev counts drop back. Latency returns ~within 3% of baseline.
Leo Kim: Good prove. But we should avoid flipping kernel preference blindly. Could add a metric to the selector: predicted writev delta for kernel+seq+bsize and penalize kernels that increase host syscalls.
Jordan Patel: Agree. Also we can add an ingress coalescer: short-term buffer on host that waits up to X ms or Y bytes before writev when latency budget allows. That might avoid swapping kernels.
Maria Chen: Any KV cache evidence? Maybe new kernel's prepare_kv_shard touches shards more frequently leading to lock contention.
Sam Torres: Not seeing lock contention in perf counters; kvcache hit rate stable. This is mainly framing/serialize overhead.
Leo Kim: Then minimal changes: (1) update kernel selector scoring to include host_writev_penalty (we can estimate from microbench); (2) deploy a micro-coalesce toggle in proxy to batch small frames for <2ms; (3) run a canary.
Jordan Patel: For scoring: we need a small matrix: kernel x seq_bucket x batch_size -> expected writes_per_token. We can compute from offline microbench harness and feed into selector config.
Sam Torres: I already ran microbench and have a CSV: kernel,seq_bucket,bsize,writes_per_req,median_host_ms. I'll drop into the perf bucket (link internal/data/1764141414/microbench.csv).
Maria Chen: Cool. Who owns the selector change? I can write the config + scoring patch. Sam can add a unit test to the selector using the CSV. Leo can prototype the proxy coalescer toggle.
Sam Torres: Sounds good. I'll also add a debug-trace for writev counts on host so we can monitor during canary.
perf-bot: Canary checklist: create canary route with kernel_override=legacy-attn for seq<128, enable coalescer=false -> monitor host_writev_rate, host_p95; duration 2h.
Jordan Patel: If that stabilizes, rollout plan: update scoring weighting to penalize >30% write increase, then revert kernel swap in full rollout only if scoring still picks it.
Leo Kim: For the proxy coalescer: I'll add config: coalesce_ms and coalesce_bytes, default 0ms/0b in prod. For canary set coalesce_ms=2ms.
Sam Torres: Great. Also note we should include grpc write path; adding small buffer there too.
Maria Chen: I'll push selector PR later today. Sam, can you open the canary and post route id?
Sam Torres: Will do. Route: route-rt-176414 (canary). Starting canary in 10m.
Jordan Patel: One more ask: add a lightweight e2e that simulates short-chat QPS and asserts writev/request <2.8. Plumb it into CI gating for kernel selector changes.
Sam Torres: Yep adding e2e now. Will update thread when canary is up. :thumbsup:
Maria Chen: Thanks team. This looked subtle — kernel changes are not GPU-only.
Leo Kim: Agreed. Lesson: include host framing heuristics in kernel perf matrix.
Sam Torres: Canary started. Monitoring dashboard: internal/dash/host_writev?route=route-rt-176414
perf-bot: Canary live. Monitoring host_writev_rate, host_p95_latency, kvcache_hits.
Sam Torres: Early signal (5m): writev_rate down ~45% vs previous baseline, p95 trending down. Will keep monitoring for 2h.
Maria Chen: Nice. Marking this triage as ownership: selector + proxy coalesce. Follow-up retro once stable.
Sam Torres: Closing for now, will paste final numbers in ~2h.
